notes: SHIP v1.14.414 - INGEST GUARDS: A REQUIRED SHEET THAT CONTRIBUTES NOTHING IS NO LONGER REPORTED AS SUCCESS, AND A HOST-LESS MASTER CAN NO LONGER ERASE A POPULATED ONE. These three defects were found while investigating the v1.14.411 field report. NONE of them caused it - that turned out to be honest data, row s4 cabled and not yet provisioned - but the investigation could not distinguish honest data from lost data quickly, and these are the reasons why. All three are proven with a working reproduction, not reasoned about. GUARD 1 - PARSED NOW MEANS CONTRIBUTED ROWS, NOT WAS PRESENT. stats.sheetsParsed was a STATIC list: SITE-HOSTS appeared in it whether it yielded four thousand hosts or none. Reproduced end to end - a Master whose SITE-HOSTS column D is shifted one place parses to 24 cabs / 0 hosts / 24 cables and reported EXACTLY the same sheetsParsed as the healthy control that yielded 144 hosts. A required sheet that reads as success while contributing zero rows is a silent failure in a required input. There are three buckets now, because absent and present-but-empty are different facts and only one is a problem: parsed (found AND produced rows), sheetsEmpty (found and produced NOTHING - the real signal), sheetsSkipped (never read, by design or absent). sheetsSkipped keeps its old meaning so no reader breaks - and nothing read any of them, which was itself the problem: the accounting was invisible. GUARD 1b - IT NOW REACHES GLASS. The only report of an empty required sheet was a console line, invisible on the iPhone this app is used on: the operator saw an import that looked entirely successful and found out at the next cold start. An empty required sheet now raises a toast on the attention channel naming WHICH sheet came back empty, with the cab and host counts. Stated as a fact rather than an error, deliberately: a Master with no hosts is legitimate for a row that is cabled and not yet provisioned - exactly the case that cost a sprint - so PHANTOM names what it found and leaves the judgement to the person who knows the site. GUARD 2 - A HOST-LESS MASTER MAY NOT SILENTLY ERASE A POPULATED ONE. phantom_master_v1 holds ONE generation with no history and no automatic backup, and save() guarded only on racksByCab EXISTING, which a cable-only parse satisfies perfectly. So a mis-exported file - one drifted column is enough - overwrote a working Master and the operator learned about it on the next cold start. save() now refuses that specific transition and says so on both channels. REFUSING TO PERSIST COSTS NOTHING IN-SESSION: the caller assigns window._lastPhantomMaster regardless, so the newly imported Master is fully live until the app restarts; what is refused is the destruction of the stored one. A host-less Master on a CLEAN slate is still accepted - verified - because a cabled unprovisioned row is legitimate data and the guard must not make a legitimate import impossible. The escape is deliberate and already existed: phantom_clearMaster() then re-import. GUARD 3 - THE COUNTS ARE PERSISTED. The parse recorded totalHosts and totalCables and the storage whitelist dropped both, so a RESTORED Master could not state its own emptiness: the app had no way to tell this Master genuinely has no hosts from the hosts were lost. That ambiguity is precisely what turned an honest 0/0 into a full investigation. Two integers, additive and optional - load() validates only schemaVersion, so payloads written before this ship restore fine and simply report unknown counts. ONE COUNTER, BOTH SHAPES: hostCount() counts from racksByCab so it works identically on a fresh parseResult and on a restored payload. The overwrite guard compares the two, and a counter that read stats on one and racks on the other could disagree with itself - the same arity/shape trap that produced the v1.14.348 bug. VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, against the app's own parser and store: good Master saves (144 hosts stored); host-less Master REFUSED with the stored Master still reading 144 hosts and still named GOOD.xlsx; host-less Master on a clean slate ACCEPTED; sheetsParsed [CUTSHEET, SITE-HOSTS] with empty [] for the healthy file versus [CUTSHEET] with empty [SITE-HOSTS] for the shifted one; totalHosts 144 and totalCables 24 both surviving the round trip. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4579/4579 balanced, CRLF intact with 0 lone LF, 0 lone CR and 0 control bytes, three-stamp lockstep. No UI surface changed; no RACK SCENE LOCK term touched; ?legacy=1 unaffected. DEVICE-VERIFY: clear the service-worker cache, confirm v1.14.414, then re-import your CURRENT Master and confirm it still loads and still reports its real cab count. If a Master ever imports with a sheet that contributed nothing you will now see a toast naming that sheet - that is the guard working, not a new fault.
